attempts.summary: Configured node1 (VyOS) as a NAT gateway for the private "lan" network (10.50.50.0/24, egress:false) so node2 and node3 can reach the internet through it, implemented entirely via an Ansible playbook run from the designated control_node (node4). node1's eth1 got a static LAN address (10.50.50.1/24) plus a masquerade source-NAT rule out eth0; node2/node3's enp8s0 got static LAN addresses and a low-priority (metric 200) default route via node1, leaving their existing mgmt-network default route (metric 100) untouched so management/exec access was never disrupted. Diagnosed and fixed a strict rp_filter drop on the LAN interfaces that was silently discarding de-NATed return traffic (classic asymmetric-route RPF issue). Verified end-to-end egress from node2/node3 via the private interface specifically (HTTP 204 from a live internet endpoint), confirmed idempotent playbook re-runs, and completed the mandatory one-at-a-time restart protocol on all four managed nodes with boot-id-verified restarts and full post-restart recovery — including fixing a VyOS SSH-key reconciler issue where the login config (not just the authorized_keys file) must hold the cluster SSH key or it gets wiped on every boot.
